articles.title: KloudMate Unveils India's First Agentic Observability Platform with Auto-RCA and Self ...
articles.content: VMPL Bengaluru (Karnataka) [India], August 24: Unplanned downtime across cloud infrastructure, applications, and networks costs enterprises between $5,000 and $7,500 per minute; a significant financial hemorrhage according to industry benchmarks. For digital-first businesses, that figure compounds even faster, resulting in disrupted transactions, eroded customer trust, and engineering teams that are forever consumed by firefighting. AI-native Auto-RCA and Self-Healing Workflows compress incident resolution cycles by upto 50%, optimize operational expenditure, and reclaim engineering time lost to reactive firefighting. Bengaluru & Texas-based deeptech startup, KloudMate, today announced the launch of its Agentic Observability suite, an AI-native observability platform that detects, investigates, and autonomously resolves incidents, compressing resolution times from hours to seconds. The launch positions KloudMate among a select group of global technology providers pioneering agentic AI within enterprise-grade observability ecosystems, and marks a pivotal moment for India's fast evolving enterprise technology story. The suite introduces natural-language querying, Smart Alert Grouping, and Automated Root Cause Analysis (Auto-RCA) with Autonomous Triage, engineered to attack the two primary metrics that define operational economics: Mean-Time-to-Resolution (MTTR) and engineering productivity. In most early deployments, customers have seen MTTR drop by upto 50% and alert noise reduce by upto 70%, while significantly increasing monitoring their coverage. Extending this intelligence into action, KloudMate has also introduced 'Workflows', a visual, drag-and-drop orchestration engine that lets engineering teams design automated response playbooks for their infrastructure and applications. Workflows enables teams to pre-define deterministic sequences of remediation actions, such as restarting a service, scaling a resource, or rotating a credential, that execute automatically the moment a condition is met (or subject to engineer sign-off for critical workflows). Human judgment stays in the loop; the toil does not. A New Paradigm in Observability, SRE-Ops & Incident Management Traditionally, observability platforms have functioned as passive repositories of telemetry data, i.e. logs, metrics, and traces, that engineers must manually correlate during high-pressure outages. KloudMate's new suite reverses this paradigm entirely. The moment an anomaly is detected, the platform's AI infrastructure autonomously initiates an investigation, correlating disparate signals and surfacing a probable root cause before a human responder is even engaged. For enterprise leadership, this translates into a tangible shift: reliability stops being a cost-center that scales with headcount, and becomes an autonomous capability that scales with the business. In an environment where engineering talent is scarce and expensive, that is not a convenience. It is a competitive moat. Commenting on the launch, the founders of KloudMate, Amitava Saha, Bidyut Baruah and Pranab Buragohain unanimously echoed the same sentiments: "Observability was built to collect data. We built KloudMate to close incidents. For decades, the industry equated observability with data volume: more dashboards, more logs, more alerts, more noise. We have inverted that model. The minute an anomaly surfaces, KloudMate begins investigating, often before an engineer has even acknowledged the alert. This is not about replacing human involvement and judgment. It is about giving engineering teams a decisive headstart, backed by transparent, auditable evidence". A Milestone for Indian AI & Enterprise Tech. The announcement arrives at...

articles.title: Non-GMO Popcorn Maize Hybrid Seed: What Is It? C. P. Radhakrishnan to Launch India's First Seed
articles.content: Popcorn is one of the most popular snacks not only in India but worldwide also. Behind every bowl of popcorn, there are special varieties of maize grown. As per the PIB , on August 24, 2026, Vice President of India C. P. Radhakrishnan will visit Musunuru in the Eluru district of Andhra Pradesh. During his visit, he will attend a program held at the Gourmet Popcornica Factory, where he will launch India’s first Non-GMO High-Expansion Popcorn Maize Hybrid Seed. So, this is very important for students who are preparing for competitive exams like UOSC, SSC, Railways, or any state exams; these questions may be asked in these exams that what is a new popcorn maize seed? What does non-GMO mean, what is a hybrid seed, and why is it called high-expansion popcorn maize? Let’s understand all these basic questions in simple terms. Key Facts Aspects Facts What is being launched? India’s first non-GMO high-expansion popcorn maize hybrid seed Who will launch it? Vice President C. P. Radhakrishnan When? August 24, 2026 Where? Musunuru, Eluru district, Andhra Pradesh Venue Gourmet Popcornica Factory What type of seed is it? Non-GMO hybrid popcorn maize seed What does high-expansion mean? The popcorn kernels can expand well when heated Vice President C. P. Radhakrishnan will visit Musunuru village in Eluru, Andhra Pradesh, today. ▪️He will launch India’s first non-Genetically Modified Organism (GMO) high-expansion popcorn maize hybrid seed in Musunuru. ▪️He will also felicitate farmers and address… pic.twitter.com/LtI0zcKFsw — All India Radio News (@airnewsalerts) August 24, 2026 What Is the New Non-GMO Popcorn Maize Seed? The new seed is a non-GMO high-expansion popcorn maize hybrid seed. It is especially developed for growing high maize that can be used to make popcorn fro earring in snacks. It will be launched by VP C. P. Radhakrishnan , and it is India’s first non-GMO high-expansion popcorn maize hybrid seed. It has three important features; these are: Non-GMO: It is not genetically modified through genetic engineering. Hybrid: It has been developed by just crossing selected parents, maize plants, to bring different and unique characteristics to these seeds. High Expansion: These maize kernels are expected to expand to a high degree on a larger scale when they convert into popcorn. So, these seeds were designed for growing a special type of popcorn maize rather than ordinary maize. What Is Popcorn Maize? Popcorn maize is a special type of maize whose kernels can pop when they are heated. A popcorn kernel contains a small amount of moisture inside a hard outer covering. When the kernel is heated, the water inside turns into steam, and while pressure builds inside the kernel, eventually the outer covering breaks open. The inside then turns into the familiar soft and fluffy popcorn. This is why not every type of maize can make good popcorn . Popcorn maize has special characteristics that allow it to pop properly. articles.title: India Plans Bharatiya Antariksha Station by 2035 - GKToday
articles.content: Home India Plans Bharatiya Antariksha Station by 2035 India Plans Bharatiya Antariksha Station by 2035 August 24, 2026 Current Affairs Today - Latest Current Affairs - 2026-2027 India has approved the first module of the Bharatiya Antariksh Station (BAS), a proposed Indian space station planned for completion by 2035. The station is designed as a low-Earth orbit platform and is linked to India’s human spaceflight programme under the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO). Bharatiya Antariksh Station: Basic Features The Bharatiya Antariksh Station is planned as a 52-tonne space station in low-Earth orbit at an altitude of 400 to 450 kilometres. The station is designed to support a crew of three to four astronauts for stays of three to six months. The proposed station will consist of five modules. BAS-01 and Design Development The first module of the station is known as BAS-01. The Baseline Design Review and System Engineering for BAS-01 were completed, and 31 baseline design documents were released. The Union Cabinet approved the development of BAS-01 by extending the scope of the Gaganyaan Programme. The estimated cost of developing and launching BAS-01 is ₹1,763 crore. The expenditure is planned over four years from 2025 to 2028. ISRO’s Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre issued an Expression of Interest to Indian industries for fabrication and realisation of the module’s physical structure. Gaganyaan Programme and Related Missions The Bharatiya Antariksh Station is part of India’s broader human spaceflight roadmap. ISRO has planned eight missions, including launch vehicles and satellites, and the first uncrewed Gaganyaan mission is scheduled within the current year. Gaganyaan is India’s human spaceflight programme for sending astronauts into space. Important Facts for Exams The Bharatiya Antariksh Station is planned as India’s first space station. The station is designed for low-Earth orbit at 400 to 450 kilometres altitude. The proposed BAS will have five modules and a total mass of 52 tonnes. The Gaganyaan Programme is India’s human spaceflight programme under ISRO. Institutional and Parliamentary References The Lok Sabha received information on the BAS-01 module through written replies in 2025 and 2026. The National Level Review Committee finalised and approved the overall structural configuration of the BAS on 3 December 2025. The project is associated with ISRO, the Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre, and the Union government’s space policy framework. articles.title: Make India global hub for space startups: PM Modi
articles.content: Make India global hub for space startups: PM Modi The Hans India Update: 2026-08-24 03:14 IST Prime Minister Narendra Modi poses during an interaction session with the CEOs and founders of space startups on the National Space Day in New Delhi on Sunday New Delhi: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday called for policy consistency and a globally competitive ecosystem as he interacted with chief executives of Indian space startups, saying India should aspire to become a destination where talent from across the world comes to build its future. The Prime Minister lauded the entrepreneurs for taking risks in a relatively new sector and for placing their faith in the government following the opening up of India’s space industry to private participation. He said predictable and stable policymaking was crucial to encouraging innovation and giving entrepreneurs the confidence to pursue ambitious ventures. “Whatever decisions we take, we should remain consistent with them and should not keep changing them repeatedly,” Modi said, stressing that those taking risks should feel assured of a supportive policy environment even when they encounter setbacks. The interaction covered a wide range of technologies and ambitions, including launch vehicles, satellite propulsion, orbital services, space debris removal, in-orbit refuelling, ground station networks and pharmaceutical manufacturing in space. A Skyroot representative described the company as India’s first space-tech unicorn and spoke about the July 18 launch of India’s first private rocket, which deployed satellites. Calling the achievement only a “warm-up”, the CEO said it marked the beginning of the company’s larger journey. The company plans to undertake one launch every month by the middle of next year and has already set up three factories with the capacity to manufacture one rocket a month, the CEO said. Its longer-term ambition is to scale up to one launch a week and eventually several launches a day. Modi also sought to know whether the successful launch had improved investor confidence and opened up new opportunities for the country’s emerging private space sector. Startup leaders said investor confidence had increased, while another CEO said the company had secured eight launch contracts in the past month, most of them from international customers. “The world must now be looking for Indian startups, asking who is there in this field. Because once there is a breakthrough, people’s attention immediately turns towards it,” Modi observed. The Prime Minister also highlighted the opportunity to make India a major global hub for space talent. He noted that Indian professionals based in the US and Europe were increasingly seeking to return home and join Indian companies after the sector was opened to greater private participation. “We should create an aura that makes people across the world look to India to build their future,” Modi said, adding that people should see India as a destination for building careers in the space sector. articles.title: India's first 100% indigenised AK-203 'Sher' rifle made, test-fired at factory in UP's Amethi
articles.content: India's first 100% indigenised AK-203 ‘Sher’ rifle made, test-fired at factory in UP's Amethi “We have successfully produced and fired the first AK-203 (Sher) rifle made with 100% Indian components and input materials,” IRRPL CEO Major Gen Sharma said. Updated on: Aug 23, 2026, 23:12:56 IST By HT News Desk Prefer HT on Google Share via Copy link India has manufactured and tested a prototype of the 100 per cent indigenised AK-203 ‘Sher’ rifle, with army trials for the weapon to begin in September this year, Major General SK Sharma said on Sunday, while sharing a video of the test firing. Ever single component and input material which has gone into manufacturing the rifle is sourced from the Indian industry, Major Gen Sharma said. (LinkedIn/ Maj Gen SK Sharma, AVSM, SM(Bar), VSM) The rifles are manufactured by the Indo-Russian Rifles Private Limited, a joint-venture of the Indian Defence Public Sector Undertakings (DPSUs), along with Concern Kalashnikov and Rosoboron export from Russia. Maj Gen S K Sharma, who is the CEO and managing director of IRRPL, said the testing of the prototype was “a moment of immense pride” for the company. Also Read | Indian Army to get loitering munitions worth ₹ 1,577 crore “We have successfully produced and fired the first AK-203 (Sher) rifle made with 100% Indian components and input materials,” Major Gen Sharma said in a post on LinkedIn. ‘Every single component, input material sourced from India’ Ever single component and input material which has gone into manufacturing the rifle is sourced from the Indian industry, Major Gen Sharma said in the post. He said this was not just “localisation of selected components”, but was a “true, end-to-end ‘100% genuine indigenisation’ of the rifle.” He said the prototype of the first 100 per cent indigenised vehicle had “successfully undergone firing, including burst firing”, adding that the initial results were “extremely encouraging.” “A proud moment for IRRPL, our partners (AWEIL & OSL) and MSMEs, and the entire Indian Defence Industry. This is Atmanirbhar Bharat in action!!” Major Gen Sharma said. Also Read | India imposes phased ban on import of 405 defence items to boost domestic production ‘IRRPL moving towards production rate of one AK-203 every 100 seconds’ Major Gen Sharma said that with the successful testing of the first prototype, IRRPL would now focus on producing the requisite number of 100 per cent indigenised AK-203 ‘Sher’ rifles for trials to the Indian Armed Forces in September, 2026. The IRRPL CEO said the company will be “moving towards a production rate of one AK-203 (Sher) every 100 seconds,” adding that there is “much more ahead.” Major Gen Sharma further said that IRRPL was also looking to prepone the delivery timeline of the approximately 6 lakh rifles that it has to supply to the Indian Army “by almost one year”. He credited the company's efforts towards “capacity enhancement, indigenisation and production optimisation” for the efficiency.
